summary: Edge ingress slow‑start + upstream restart loop causing sustained 5xx elevation for dedicated customer
description:
Issue summary: Glyph Labs (dedicated) reported a sustained elevation in 5xx responses beginning ~2026-03-11 12:05 UTC. Error rates on their tenant routes spiked to 25–40% for ~50 minutes. Impact: customer-facing features (chat and embedding uploads) observed failures and timeouts; several bulk embedding jobs retried and backed off.

Impact: ~30% of Glyph traffic returned 5xx (primarily 502/503) during the window; P1 due to production impact for an enterprise-tier dedicated customer.

Environment: Production, dedicated pool for Glyph Labs in us-east1 with fallback routing to shared pool in eu-west-1.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Send sustained streaming requests at 200–300 rps against Glyph route /v1/chat with keepalive enabled.
2) Observe accept queue growth at API gateway and hedged retries.
3) Upstream serving-runtime processes begin SIGTERM/restart cycles and GPU-bound processes show nvml resets.

Observed symptoms: API gateway accept-queue growth, increased handshake latency, hedged retry amplification, upstream runtime processes entering restart loops (SIGTERM followed by fast restart), and autoscaler reacting by spinning new pods which rejoin and then restart again.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate tenant burst: 250 rps streaming requests to Glyph route in us-east1 with long-lived connections and small initial tokens; monitor apigw accept-queue and runtime pod restarts. Observe error rate rise after ~3–6 minutes of sustained load.

investigation_notes: 12:10 UTC - confirmed spike correlates with Glyph route weight bump from recent affinitization rollout (edge affinitization change deployed ~11:50 UTC).
Dashboards: apigw.accept_queue (us-east1) shows sustained >400 backlog; runtime.pod_restart_rate spiked to 7/min for Glyph pool; nvme_iowait and GPU driver resets visible on node metrics.
Trace sampling: hedged retries triggered due to initial handshake latency; majority of 5xx are 502/503 from runtime before request reaches model forward pass.

Hypothesis 1: edge affinitization changed incoming connection distribution causing hot spot on a subset of serving nodes -> OOM / GPU driver resets under concentrated load.
Hypothesis 2: a recently merged apigw change to slow-start/accept-queue thresholds (PR-289) interacts poorly with our autoscaler liveness probe and causes churn.
Test: temporarily disabled affinitization weight for Glyph at 12:25 UTC — initial drop in accept_queue and error rate fell to ~6% within 5 minutes.
comments: 2026-03-11 12:18 UTC - Aisha Patel (Support): Initial customer report received; capturing metrics and opening incident. Customer reported failures for both chat and embedding uploads. (sla escalated to P1)

2026-03-11 12:28 UTC - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Observed apigw backlog and runtime restart loops; suspect hot-spot from recent affinitization rollout. Temporarily adjusted route weight and requested rollback for affinitization.

estimated_customer_impact: Approximately 25–40% errors for Glyph Labs traffic over window; several embedding jobs failed and retried—customer reported user-visible failures in production.
resolution:
Mitigation applied: rolled back edge affinitization weight changes for Glyph Labs at 12:25 UTC and temporarily diverted a percentage of traffic to fallback shared pool in eu-west-1 to relieve hot nodes. Result: accept_queue and 5xx rates dropped to baseline within 5–8 minutes.
Root cause (working hypothesis): affinitization/edge distribution change created a hot-spot on a subset of serving nodes which, under a tenant burst, triggered GPU-driver resets and rapid restart cycles. Interacting factor: an APIGW slow-start threshold change (PR-289) made the accept-queue tolerate more backlog before shedding, which amplified hedged retries and restart churn.
Permanent actions planned:
- Revert or rework affinitization rollout to use smoother ramp and cap per-node connection rates.
- Update autoscaler and liveness probe to avoid SIGTERM race during GPU driver resets.
- Add a runtime pre-check to isolate GPU reset errors and perform graceful pause before restart.
- Postmortem and customer-facing summary to be published; schedule a hotfix for apigw slow-start thresholds (owner: apigw team, ETA 2026-03-16).
Follow-ups: create runbook entry for tenant hot-spot mitigation and add circuit-breaker thresholds for dedicated pools.
